question: Which statement best describes Always associate a label?
options: An error must be both visible and programmatically tied to its field. Link the message with aria-describedby, mark the field aria-invalid="true", and put the message in an aria-live region (polite) so screen readers announce it when it appears without moving focus.

Radio buttons and checkboxes that form one question need a group label. Wrap them in a <fieldset> and give the group a <legend> — screen readers announce the legend together with each option, so 'Express, Shipping' becomes clear instead of just 'Express'.

The required attribute enforces validation and is exposed to assistive tech in modern browsers. Add aria-required="true" when you need to convey 'required' but can't use the native attribute (e.g., a custom widget), or to maximize compatibility — but don't rely on aria-required alone for actual validation.

Every control needs a programmatic label so assistive tech announces its purpose. Use <label for="id"> matched to the input's id, or wrap the input in the label. This also enlarges the click target — clicking the label focuses the field.
explanation: Every control needs a programmatic label so assistive tech announces its purpose. Use <label for="id"> matched to the input's id, or wrap the input in the label. This also enlarges the click target — clicking the label focuses the field.
